```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

out_dir <- file.path(getwd(), "seahorse_crossed_design_analysis")
results <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "statistical_results_all_endpoints.csv"),
                    check.names = FALSE)
dat <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "seahorse_analysis_dataset.csv"),
                check.names = FALSE)

displayed <- c("baseline_ocr", "atp_linked", "maximal_ocr")
current_p <- c(baseline_ocr = 0.0246, atp_linked = 0.0294, maximal_ocr = 0.0106)

fmt_p <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_,
         ifelse(x < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 4)))
}
```

## Recommendation

The 27 EC-fibroblast combinations are not 27 independent biological donors. Disease condition is a property of the fibroblast donor (3 healthy and 6 progressive SSc donors), and each fibroblast line was tested repeatedly in the same three EC lines. The primary analysis is therefore a repeated-measures linear mixed model:

`outcome ~ fibroblast condition + EC line + (1 | fibroblast donor)`

EC line is included as a fixed blocking factor because only three specific EC lines were studied. Fibroblast donor is a random intercept. A condition-by-EC-line interaction was tested first and was not supported for any displayed endpoint. Two-sided Kenward-Roger tests provide small-sample inference across the ten fibroblast donors. An exact donor-label permutation test is reported as a distribution-light sensitivity analysis; it preserves each donor's observed EC-line measurements and adjusts for EC line.

## Primary results

```{r primary-table, echo=FALSE}
primary_table <- results %>%
  filter(endpoint %in% displayed) %>%
  mutate(
    `Current figure P` = unname(current_p[endpoint]),
    `Healthy adjusted mean` = healthy_adjusted_mean,
    `Progressive SSc adjusted mean` = ssc_adjusted_mean,
    `Difference (SSc - healthy)` = estimate_ssc_minus_healthy,
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", ci_low, ci_high),
    `Mixed-model P` = fmt_p(lmm_kenward_roger_p),
    `Holm P (3 endpoints)` = fmt_p(holm_p_three_displayed),
    `Exact donor permutation P` = fmt_p(donor_exact_permutation_p),
    `Condition x EC P` = fmt_p(condition_by_ec_interaction_p)
  ) %>%
  select(
    Endpoint = label,
    `Healthy adjusted mean`, `Progressive SSc adjusted mean`,
    `Difference (SSc - healthy)`, `95% CI`,
    `Mixed-model P`, `Holm P (3 endpoints)`,
    `Exact donor permutation P`, `Condition x EC P`, `Current figure P`
  )

primary_table %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  kable(align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(primary_table) - 1)))
```

On the raw OCR-derived values, progressive-SSc conditioned medium was associated with higher basal OCR (estimated difference 3.15, 95% CI 1.10 to 5.21; mixed-model P=0.0074) and maximal OCR (difference 5.43, 95% CI 1.09 to 9.78; P=0.0203). ATP-linked respiration was higher by 1.79 units, but its 95% CI included zero (-0.06 to 3.64; P=0.0562). After Holm correction across the three displayed endpoints, basal OCR (Holm P=0.0221) and maximal OCR (Holm P=0.0406) remained below 0.05; ATP-linked respiration did not (Holm P=0.0562).

The exact EC-adjusted donor-label permutation analysis gave P=0.0143, P=0.0333 and P=0.0238 for basal OCR, ATP-linked respiration and maximal OCR, respectively. ATP-linked respiration is therefore best described as borderline or method-sensitive rather than as an unequivocal difference.

## Replotted endpoints

Each point remains an EC-line x fibroblast-line combination for visual continuity. The statistical test nevertheless uses fibroblast donor as the repeated biological unit.

```{r primary-figure, echo=FALSE, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(out_dir, "seahorse_primary_endpoints_mixed_model.png"))
```

Vector versions are provided as SVG and PDF in the analysis output folder.

## Data-label audit

```{r design-table, echo=FALSE}
design_table <- dat %>%
  distinct(ec_line, fibroblast_observed, fibroblast_model, condition) %>%
  arrange(condition, fibroblast_model, ec_line)
kable(design_table)
```

The six progressive-SSc lines and healthy lines NH208 and NH162 occur once in every EC-line block. **NH140 and NH198 are retained as separate healthy fibroblast donors in all statistical tests.** NH140 contributes the EC-line 1 measurement, whereas NH198 contributes the EC-line 2 and 3 measurements. The mixed model and blocked permutation analysis accommodate this incomplete crossing. EC source codes 427010, 412005 and 427001 are displayed as EC lines 1, 2 and 3, respectively.

## Additional endpoints

```{r all-endpoints-table, echo=FALSE}
results %>%
  transmute(
    Endpoint = label,
    Difference = round(estimate_ssc_minus_healthy, 3),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", ci_low, ci_high),
    `Mixed-model P` = fmt_p(lmm_kenward_roger_p),
    `Exact permutation P` = fmt_p(donor_exact_permutation_p),
    `Condition x EC P` = fmt_p(condition_by_ec_interaction_p),
    `Singular fit` = singular_fit
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

## Interpretation for the figure

For panel C, replace the current P values with the mixed-model values:

- Basal OCR: **P=0.0074**
- ATP-linked respiration: **P=0.0562**
- Maximal OCR: **P=0.0203**

Suggested legend wording: "P values were calculated using linear mixed-effects models with fibroblast condition and EC line as fixed effects and fibroblast donor as a random intercept; denominator degrees of freedom were estimated using the Kenward-Roger method. NH140 and NH198 were treated as separate healthy fibroblast donors. Points represent individual EC-line x fibroblast-line combinations (9 combinations from four healthy fibroblast donors and 18 combinations from six progressive-SSc fibroblast donors)."

The workbook contains Seahorse-derived endpoints only. It does not contain the extracellular-lactate measurements shown in panel B, so the displayed lactate P=0.019 was not recalculated here.

## Reproducibility

The analysis is generated by `analyze_seahorse_crossed_design.R`. Machine-readable model results, donor means, design counts, plots and model summaries are stored in `seahorse_crossed_design_analysis`.
